opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047), full-time Payroll Specialist, requests admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max at write unless their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the max is read. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requests admin on Source Code. Admin is not permitted: as a Payroll Specialist, he does not own the Source Code system (so full-time admin rule does not apply), and contractors never receive admin. The HR note lists him as full-time (max write), while the Security note lists him as a contractor with basic training (max read). Given the conflicting employee records, I apply the more restrictive maximum from Security (contractor, basic training → read) consistent with least privilege, and grant the maximum since the requested admin exceeds it.
